patient.name: Marcus Webb
patient.chiefComplaint: Right lower leg pinned under collapsed pallet racking, severe pain

history.hpi: Warehouse worker found with his right leg pinned from mid-shin down under a collapsed section of pallet racking after a forklift operation went wrong. Coworkers attempted to lift the rack manually without success before calling 911. Entrapment time is approximately 35 minutes and climbing while fire/rescue rigs airbags and cribbing. Patient is alert, in severe pain, denies loss of consciousness or head strike.
history.lastOralIntake: Coffee, approximately 6 hours prior to the incident
history.events: Pallet rack collapsed during forklift operation, pinning patient's right lower leg; coworkers called 911 immediately and attempted an unsuccessful manual lift before EMS/fire arrived

scene.dispatch: 45-year-old male, industrial accident, leg trapped under machinery, conscious and breathing
scene.location: Warehouse loading dock; collapsed pallet racking pinning patient's lower leg; fire department on scene coordinating extrication
scene.safety: Unstable racking overhead; fire/rescue securing the structure and rigging airbags/cribbing before controlled lift
scene.bystanders: Coworkers present, called 911 immediately, attempted an unsuccessful manual lift before EMS arrival
visualCues: Collapsed pallet rack pinning right lower leg from mid-shin down
Patient supine on concrete, alert, gripping the edge of the pallet in visible pain
Entrapment time noted at approximately 35 minutes and climbing
Fire crew rigging airbags and cribbing for a controlled, coordinated lift

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 45-year-old male pinned under collapsed pallet racking, alert and in severe pain, with an entrapment time already exceeding 30 minutes. Fire/rescue is on scene rigging equipment for extrication but has not yet released the pressure.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in both arms and left leg; right leg immobilized under racking, unable to assess distal movement
otherFindings: Right lower leg pinned from mid-shin down, pain 9/10
No visible active hemorrhage at entrapment site
Distal right foot pulse faintly palpable, cool to touch
Denies head strike or loss of consciousness
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It's crushing my leg, please get this thing off me!"

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV access (two large-bore lines preferred)
expectedActions.rationale: Vascular access must be secured before the entrapping pressure is released.

expectedActions.shortAction: Attach cardiac monitor and obtain 12-lead EKG; watch for hyperkalemia changes
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Attach cardiac monitor. Obtain/interpret 12-lead EKG, if available. Carefully monitor for dysrhythmias or signs of hyperkalemia before and immediately after release of pressure and during transport (e.g., peaked T waves, wide QRS, lengthening QT interval, loss of P wave)
expectedActions.rationale: Hyperkalemia from crushed muscle can precipitate lethal arrhythmias at the moment of release.

expectedActions.shortAction: Administer 1,000 mL normal saline IV bolus before release (avoid lactated Ringer's)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: IV fluids should be administered prior to releasing the crushed body part. Administer 1000 mL normal saline (NS) bolus. Avoid lactated Ringer's solution as it contains potassium.
expectedActions.rationale: Pre-release volume loading blunts the hypovolemia and electrolyte shifts of reperfusion syndrome.

expectedActions.shortAction: Sodium bicarbonate 50 mEq IV over 5 min (90 kg × 1 mEq/kg = 90 mEq → capped at 50 mEq max)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For significant crush injuries or prolonged entrapment of an extremity, consider sodium bicarbonate 1 mEq/kg (maximum dose of 50 mEq) IV bolus over 5 minutes
expectedActions.rationale: Alkalinization reduces the risk of myoglobin-related renal injury and helps counter impending hyperkalemia.

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 90 mcg IV (90 kg × 1 mcg/kg; max initial dose 100 mcg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Adequate analgesia is needed before and during a painful, prolonged extrication.

transitions.if: IV fluids and bicarb given before release
transitions.condition: Crew establishes IV access, administers a 1,000 mL normal saline bolus and sodium bicarbonate, attaches cardiac monitoring, and provides analgesia before fire/rescue releases the entrapping pressure.
Fire/rescue releases the racking before the crew has completed IV fluid resuscitation, precipitating an unbuffered reperfusion event.

phases.name: IV fluids and bicarb given before release
phases.description: Crew establishes IV access and administers fluids, sodium bicarbonate, and analgesia while fire/rescue continues rigging for a controlled release, per the crush injury protocol's requirement that fluids precede release of the entrapping pressure.
phases.triggerCondition: Recognizing prolonged entrapment as a crush injury mechanism, the crew prioritizes IV fluid resuscitation and sodium bicarbonate before the crushed limb is released, while coordinating pain control and continuous cardiac monitoring.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, skin warming, diaphoresis improving
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in both arms and left leg; right leg still pinned, distal sensation intact per patient report
otherFindings: Cardiac monitor attached, no ectopy noted
Fire crew continuing to rig airbags for controlled lift
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That helps some. How much longer until it's off?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Continuously monitor EKG for peaked T waves, widening QRS during and after release
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Carefully monitor for dysrhythmias or signs of hyperkalemia before and immediately after release of pressure and during transport (e.g., peaked T waves, wide QRS, lengthening QT interval, loss of P wave)
expectedActions.rationale: The moment of release is when reperfusion-driven hyperkalemia is most likely to manifest.

expectedActions.shortAction: Continue normal saline infusion through and after extrication
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Continue fluid resuscitation through extrication and transfer to hospital
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing volume support is required as reperfusion continues to shift fluid and electrolytes.

transitions.condition: With fluids, bicarbonate, and monitoring in place, the crew coordinates with fire/rescue for a controlled release of the crushing pressure.

phases.name: Extrication coordinated after fluids given
phases.description: Fire/rescue performs a controlled lift of the racking while the crew maintains fluid resuscitation and watches the cardiac monitor closely for signs of hyperkalemia as the crushed leg is released.
phases.triggerCondition: With adequate pre-release fluid resuscitation and bicarbonate on board, fire/rescue proceeds with a controlled release of the pallet racking while the crew continuously monitors the EKG for peaked T waves, widening QRS, or other hyperkalemic changes.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial and pedal pulses present bilaterally, skin warm and pink
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right leg now free; decreased sensation distally, unable to actively move foot
otherFindings: Racking lifted in a controlled fashion by fire crew
Right lower leg visibly deformed with mottled skin, no active hemorrhage
EKG monitored continuously through release, no ectopy or peaked T waves noted so far
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It's off — oh man, that's a weird feeling."

expectedActions.shortAction: Continue normal saline infusion at 500–1,000 mL/hr post-extrication
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Continued resuscitation with normal saline (500–1000 mL/hr for adults, 10 mL/kg/hr for children)
expectedActions.rationale: Sustained fluid support continues to mitigate delayed rhabdomyolysis-related complications.

expectedActions.shortAction: Rapid transport to a trauma center; reassess neurovascular status and pain en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Rapid extrication and evacuation to a definitive care facility (trauma center preferred)
expectedActions.rationale: Definitive management of crush injury and monitoring for delayed complications requires trauma center resources.

transitions.condition: The EKG remains free of peaked T waves or QRS widening after release, and the patient remains hemodynamically stable.
Shortly after release, the EKG develops peaked T waves and a widening QRS consistent with hyperkalemia from the reperfused limb.

phases.name: Stable release, no hyperkalemia signs
phases.description: The patient remains hemodynamically stable after release with no EKG evidence of hyperkalemia. The crew continues fluid resuscitation and prepares for rapid transport to a trauma center.
phases.triggerCondition: With no hyperkalemic changes on the monitor and stable vitals following release, the crew continues supportive fluids and packages the patient for transport.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial and pedal pulses present bilaterally, skin warm and pink
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right leg splinted; decreased distal sensation persists, being monitored
otherFindings: Pain improved to 3/10 with fentanyl and splinting
Right leg splinted and dressed, no active bleeding
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel a lot better now. Thanks for getting me out."

phases.name: Release attempted before fluids
phases.description: Fire/rescue releases the racking before adequate IV fluids were given, producing an abrupt reperfusion event: sudden hypotension, tachycardia, and diaphoresis as unbuffered potassium and toxins wash into circulation.
phases.triggerCondition: Because the crew did not complete fluid resuscitation before the release, the sudden reperfusion of the crushed limb causes acute hypovolemia and electrolyte shifts, precipitating hemodynamic instability.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak and thready, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right leg free but flaccid; sensation diminished
otherFindings: Sudden drop in blood pressure immediately after release
EKG showing early peaked T waves
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel really dizzy all of a sudden..."

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize reperfusion syndrome: sudden hypotension and arrhythmia risk after release without adequate fluids
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Sudden release of a crushed extremity may result in reperfusion syndrome (acute hypovolemia, electrolyte abnormalities, and subsequent lethal arrhythmia)
expectedActions.rationale: Rapid recognition allows the crew to escalate to aggressive fluid and hyperkalemia treatment before arrest occurs.

phases.name: Peaked T waves recognized post-release
phases.description: The EKG develops peaked T waves and a widening QRS shortly after a properly fluid-resuscitated release, prompting immediate hyperkalemia treatment.
phases.triggerCondition: Despite pre-release fluids and bicarbonate, the reperfused limb releases enough potassium to produce peaked T waves and QRS widening on the monitor, requiring active hyperkalemia treatment.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, skin warm, mild diaphoresis
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Right leg free and splinted; decreased distal sensation
otherFindings: Peaked T waves and QRS widening noted on monitor shortly after release
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "My heart feels like it's racing a bit."

expectedActions.shortAction: Calcium chloride 1 g IV over 5 min (ensure IV patency; do not exceed 1 mL/min)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Calcium chloride – 1 gm IV/IO over 5 minutes, ensure IV patency and do not exceed 1 mL per minute
expectedActions.rationale: Calcium stabilizes the cardiac membrane against the arrhythmogenic effects of rising potassium.

expectedActions.shortAction: Consider albuterol 5 mg nebulized for hyperkalemia; may repeat if no response
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If EKG suggestive of hyperkalemia, consider albuterol 5 mg via small volume nebulizer (can be repeated if no response is seen)
expectedActions.rationale: Beta-agonists shift potassium intracellularly, providing adjunctive temporizing treatment.
